is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. coluzzii, An. arabiensis, An. gambiae s.s.) in Northern Ghana.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc-1014F, Vgsc-1014S, Vgsc-1575Y, GSTe2-114T, and Ace1-119S (Table 1 and Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 1 provides frequencies of resistance alleles in F1 An. coluzzii populations based on insecticide resistance phenotypes (dead and alive) with N values. Table 2 provides frequencies of resistance alleles in wild F0 indoor and outdoor An. gambiae s.l. populations with N values.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from two rural communities in Northern Ghana (Kpalsogu and Libga) in 2017.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical field study conducted by the authors.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in Kpalsogu and Libga, Northern Ghana.

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a specific, new collection of mosquitoes in 2017 for this research.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the association between insecticide resistance and resting behaviour of Anopheles gambiae s.l. in Northern Ghana. It found that while phenotypic resistance was higher in indoor-resting mosquitoes, genotypic resistance markers (Vgsc-1014F, Vgsc-1575Y, GSTe2-114T, Ace1-119S) and metabolic enzyme activities were often higher in outdoor-resting populations.
